Speaking as someone without a father, it gets easier as you get older. You grow, you know who you are a little more. These things matter less when you know that it is what it is. What he said to you may seem very insensitive, but really he's right. What can he do to make up for those lost years? How much will saying "sorry" really help? A single, or even a few words doesn't undo countless years.

Conversely, if it feels like he's not committing to being a parent, then it's time to take some control and quit contact. He'll do you more damage in disappointing you than he ever did abandoning you. You don't need him to be whole. I spent a *lot* of years feeling like half of myself was missing when I should have realized that I am not my parents, either of them. 

I'm me, and I am more than my fathers absence.
